claims.text: Transition-metal catalytic activity and selectivity are governed by the energy and occupancy of catalyst d-states.
An optimal d-band-center position produces balanced adsorption of reaction intermediates.
Balanced intermediate adsorption enhances activity and selectivity while avoiding detrimental over-binding.
Pristine Pt, Pd, and Ni catalysts have different natural d-band-center positions.
Alloying or doping a transition metal with a secondary metal can systematically shift its d-band center.
The position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level influences the adsorption strength of key reaction intermediates.
Doping or alloying alters the catalyst electronic structure and d-band-center position.
Changing the d-band-center position changes the binding energies of adsorbed intermediates.
An optimally shifted d-band center provides sufficient adsorption for catalysis without poisoning caused by excessively strong binding.
Catalysts having the optimal d-band-center position will exhibit greater catalytic activity than unmodified catalysts.
Catalysts having the optimal d-band-center position will exhibit better selectivity than unmodified catalysts.
Systematic variation of dopant level will produce volcano-shaped turnover-frequency behavior.
Systematic variation of dopant level will produce volcano-shaped selectivity behavior.
The proposed relationship should apply primarily to transition-metal catalysts under moderate reaction conditions.
The proposed relationship may fail under very high temperatures or pressures.
The proposed relationship may fail when support effects dominate catalytic behavior.
The proposed relationship may fail when nanoparticle-size effects dominate catalytic behavior.
The influence of the d-band center on catalytic behavior is a well-discussed concept.
The quantitative relationship between d-band-center position and activity or selectivity in the targeted process has not been rigorously established.
